newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish metals union calls for FinMin EMU nod - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish metals union calls for FinMin EMU nod - paper.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink must step forward and take the lead in a definite yes-line for membership of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), chairman of the metals union Goran Johnsson said.
"He can push a yes-line from his professional role as finance minister," Johnsson said in an interview with daily newspaper Svenska Dagbladet.
"(Prime Minister) Goran Persson said plainly when he was finance minister that we should go into EMU for economic reasons."
According to Johnsson it was not possible to turn a sceptical Social Democratic party opinion to a strong EMU approval at the ruling party's congress in September.
But with a strong 'yes' line it might be possible to swing the congress to a wait-and-see line, he said.
Johnsson said he was in favour of EMU membership but underlined that he has not thought through the issue completely.
He believed that if Sweden chose not to join, costs would appear in the form of higher interest rates and a poorer wage development.
The big risk of going into EMU is, according to Johnsson, the Swedish industries' dollar dependence.
"I don't think we can remain outside EMU if, in the long term, we want to be a strong industrial country," Johnsson said.
